summary: Quantum subspace expansion (QSE) offers promising avenues to perform spectral calculations on quantum processors but comes with a large measurement overhead. Informationally complete measurements, such as classical shadows, were recently proposed to overcome this bottleneck. Here, we report the firs…

summary: Understanding flux string dynamics can provide insight into quark confinement and hadronization. First-principles quantum and numerical simulations have mostly focused on toy-model Abelian lattice gauge theories (LGTs). summary: From coating curved parts to creeping lava, thin-film gravitational drainage over complex surfaces can produce abrupt accumulation, usually associated with sharp edges or defects. Here, experiments, simulations, and asymptotics show that a smooth saddle alone generates a logarithmically singular rid…

We introduce a thermodynamically consistent constant-potential MLP (TCCP-MLP) tr…

summary: Liquid foams are archetypal athermal amorphous solids whose elasticity arises from the jamming of densely packed bubbles. We investigate the stress relaxation of nonaging liquid foams following flow cessation, using fast x-ray tomorheoscopy. Thanks to in situ , time-resolved measurements, we uncover …

title: Nonsymmorphic Time-Reversal-Doubled Axion Insulators
summary: Extension of time-reversal-doubled axion insulators to nonsymmorphic crystals establishes a spin-resolved classification scheme and identifies mixed bismuth monohalides as candidate materials.

title: Non-Abelian Quantum Signal Processing: A Composite Pulse for Fast Analytic Control of Hybrid Oscillator-Qubit Processors
summary: Researchers extend quantum signal processing to noncommuting control variables, enabling analytical control of hybrid oscillator-qubit quantum processors.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qubit Quantum Processors: Simulating Fermions, Bosons, and Gauge Fields
summary: Researchers develop a hybrid qubit-boson quantum processor framework to simulate interacting fermions, bosons, and lattice gauge fields.

title: Energy-Efficient Control of Interacting Microscopic Systems: When Longer Paths Save Energy
summary: Harnessing hydrodynamic interactions offers a route to control multiparticle systems efficiently, enabling substantial reductions in the energetic cost of microscopic transport.

title: Fractional Quantum Hall States under Density Decoherence
summary: Statistical mechanics mappings reveal that quantum information stored in the non-Abelian anyons of Moore-Read states resists arbitrary density dephasing, whereas that stored in the Laughlin states has an infinite robustness only above a critical filling factor.

title: Interaction-Assisted Topological Pumping in Few- and Many-Atom Rydberg Arrays
summary: Strong dipolar interactions in Rydberg atom arrays are found to be able to bind particles into correlated pairs and clusters that undergo efficient topological pumping along a synthetic dimension.

title: Reversibility, Chaos, and Attractors in Periodically Sheared Elastic Filaments
summary: Combining experiments on actin filaments with numerical simulations, a previously unknown transition from reversible motion to intermittent, noise-driven chaos in single semiflexible filaments under periodic shear is unveiled.

title: Overcoming Intrinsic Material Limitations through Cavity Feedback
summary: Active dissipation control via a feedback loop overcomes intrinsic magnetic losses, achieving strong coupling among photons, magnons, and phonons in cavity magnomechanics.

title: Quantum Thermal State Preparation for Near-Term Quantum Processors
summary: Researchers develop an algorithm that prepares many-body quantum thermal states accurately by combining bath resetting and modulated coupling.

title: Observing the Spatial and Temporal Evolution of Exciton Wave Functions in Organic Semiconductors
summary: Femtosecond time-resolved photoemission orbital tomography tracks photoelectron profiles to reconstruct the real-space distribution and internal quantum phase of excitons in an organic semiconductor.

title: Revealing Electron-Ytterbium Interactions through Rydberg Molecular Spectroscopy
summary: Precision spectroscopy of giant ytterbium Rydberg molecules provides a powerful new window into fundamental atomic properties, laying essential groundwork for future experiments with divalent atoms.

title: Unraveling Non-polymorphic Phase Evolution in Mg-Ag-Sb for Designing Thermally Recoverable Thermoelectrics
summary: Thermal degradation in MgAgSb thermoelectric material can be reversed with low-temperature annealing.

title: Evolution of Polycrystallinity in Homogeneously Nucleated Colloidal Crystals
summary: Direct observations of the birth and growth of polycrystalline colloidal crystals clarify the role of grain formation, a key aspect in understanding and tuning the properties of polycrystalline materials.

title: Non-Hermitian Bethe-Salpeter Equation for Open Systems: Emergence of Exceptional Points in Excitonic Spectra from First Principles
summary: Extension of the Bethe-Salpeter equation to open quantum systems predicts that engineered photonic environments induce exceptional points in the excitonic spectra of transition-metal dichalcogenides, providing a pathway for non-Hermitian quantum devices with controllable optical and valleytronic properties.

title: Leading and Beyond Leading-Order Spectral Form Factor in Chaotic Quantum Many-Body Systems Across All Dyson Symmetry Classes
summary: Researchers analytically calculate the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.
